# select_monitor (Resource)

A monitor: a scheduled query that sends an alert or a digest to one or more destinations when its trigger condition is met.

## About

A monitor runs a query on a schedule and sends a message to its destinations when its trigger fires. To learn more, see the [SELECT documentation](https://select.dev/docs/getting-started).

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/monitors`. The `api_key` configured on the provider must carry the `monitors:read` and `monitors:write` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A budget monitor: it emails when actual spend passes 80% and 100% of the
# budget.
resource "select_monitor" "budget" {
  name        = "Acme Monthly budget"
  data_source = "budget"
  state       = "enabled"
  schedule    = "daily"
  budget_id   = select_budget.monthly_org_wide.id

  destination_ids = [select_email_alert_destination.finance.id]

  notification_frequency_config = {
    frequency_type = "on_trigger"
  }

  trigger_config = {
    type = "budget_threshold"
    thresholds = [
      { metric = "actual_spend", unit = "percent", value = 80 },
      { metric = "actual_spend", unit = "percent", value = 100 },
    ]
  }

  message_config_json = jsonencode({
    sections = [
      { section_type = "title" },
    ]
  })
}

# A condition monitor: it posts to Slack when daily spend is more than 5000.
# GET /v2/monitors/query-classes lists the query classes and their columns.
resource "select_monitor" "daily_spend" {
  name        = "Daily spend above 5000"
  data_source = "organization_spend"
  state       = "enabled"
  schedule    = "daily"

  destination_ids = [select_slack_alert_destination.alerts.id]

  notification_frequency_config = {
    frequency_type     = "limit_x_days"
    frequency_interval = 1
  }

  trigger_config = {
    type      = "condition"
    operator  = ">"
    threshold = 5000
    trigger   = "on_condition_met"
    query_json = jsonencode({
      query_class  = "OrgDailySpendQuery"
      query_object = { measures = ["spend"] }
      period       = { period = 1, grain = "day" }
    })
  }

  message_config_json = jsonencode({
    sections = [
      { section_type = "title" },
      {
        section_type = "chart"
        query = {
          query_class  = "OrgDailySpendQuery"
          query_object = { measures = ["spend"] }
          period       = { period = 30, grain = "day" }
        }
      },
    ]
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `data_source` (String) The data the monitor reads. `custom` runs the monitor's own SQL, and requires a `custom_sql_results` section carrying it in `custom_sql_query`, and a `snowflake_account_id` to run it against.
- `destination_ids` (Set of String) The ids of the alert destinations the monitor sends to. Use the `id` of a `select_slack_alert_destination`, `select_email_alert_destination` or `select_ms_teams_alert_destination`.
- `message_config_json` (String) The message the monitor sends, as a JSON-encoded `MonitorMessageConfig`: `{"title": ..., "sections": [...]}`. Use `jsonencode()`. SELECT adds defaults and generated text, such as a chart title. These additions do not show as a change. A change to a key that the configuration sets shows as a change.
- `name` (String) The monitor's name, as it appears in the feed.
- `notification_frequency_config` (Attributes) How often the monitor can send a notification. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notification_frequency_config))
- `schedule` (String) How often the monitor runs. `cron` reads `cron` for the schedule.
- `state` (String) Whether the monitor runs. A `disabled` or `snoozed` monitor is not scheduled.
- `trigger_config` (Attributes) When the monitor sends. `type` selects the variant. The fields that each type requires or accepts: `digest` requires skip_if_empty. `condition` requires query_json, operator, threshold and trigger. `anomaly_prophet` requires query_json and sensitivity, and accepts trigger_on_upper_band, trigger_on_lower_band and minimum_threshold. `anomaly_percentile` requires query_json, and accepts upper_percentile, lower_percentile, deviations and minimum_threshold. `budget_threshold` requires thresholds and accepts query_json. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger_config))

### Optional

- `budget_id` (String) The budget this monitor watches. Null on a monitor that watches something other than a budget.
- `cron` (String) The cron expression the monitor runs on, in UTC. Required when `schedule` is `cron`, which only a monitor whose `data_source` is `custom` may use; null otherwise.
- `display_in_feed` (Boolean) Whether the monitor's runs appear in the monitors feed.
- `partition_columns` (List of String) The titles of the query columns that split the monitor into one alert per value. Null sends no partition config.
- `snowflake_account_id` (String) The Snowflake account a custom SQL monitor runs its SQL against, as listed by `/v2/snowflake-accounts`. Required when `data_source` is `custom` and null otherwise, since every other source reads the organization as a whole.
- `team_id` (String) The team that owns this monitor. Null leaves it to the organization, or to `snowflake_account_id` when that is set. Requires permission to write monitors for that team.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) RFC 3339 UTC creation timestamp.
- `created_by` (String) Who created the monitor.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this monitor. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The monitor's identifier in SELECT, assigned when it is created. Use it with `terraform import` to bring an existing monitor under management.
- `status` (String) What the monitor is doing now. `disabled` or `snoozed` when its `state` stops it running; otherwise how its most recent run ended, or `new` when it has not run yet.
- `type` (String) What kind of check the monitor runs. The same value as `trigger_config.type`, lifted out so it can be filtered and read without parsing the configuration.
- `update_time` (String) RFC 3339 UTC last-update timestamp.
- `updated_by` (String) Who last changed the monitor. Null if no one has since it was created.

<a id="nestedatt--notification_frequency_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notification_frequency_config`

Required:

- `frequency_type` (String) `on_trigger` sends each time the trigger fires. `on_status_change` sends when the status changes. `limit_x_hours`, `limit_x_days`, `limit_x_weeks` and `limit_x_months` send at most once per `frequency_interval` units.

Optional:

- `frequency_interval` (Number) The number of units between notifications. Required for, and only valid with, a `limit_x_*` frequency_type.


<a id="nestedatt--trigger_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger_config`

Required:

- `type` (String) The trigger variant.

Optional:

- `deviations` (Number) For `anomaly_percentile`: the number of deviations past the band, from 0 to 10.
- `lower_percentile` (Number) For `anomaly_percentile`: the lower percentile of the band, from 0 to 100.
- `minimum_threshold` (Number) For `anomaly_prophet` and `anomaly_percentile`: ignore an anomaly below this value.
- `operator` (String) For `condition`: how the query result is compared with threshold.
- `query_json` (String) The semantic-layer query the trigger evaluates, as a JSON-encoded `MonitorQuery`: `{"query_class": ..., "query_object": {...}, "period": {...}}`. Use `jsonencode()`. `GET /v2/monitors/query-classes` lists the query classes. SELECT adds defaults, such as `period.date_column`. These additions do not show as a change.
- `sensitivity` (Number) For `anomaly_prophet`: the width of the expected band, from 0 to 50.
- `skip_if_empty` (Boolean) For `digest`: true skips a digest that has no data.
- `threshold` (Number) For `condition`: the value the query result is compared with.
- `thresholds` (Attributes List) For `budget_threshold`: the spend levels that cause a send. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger_config--thresholds))
- `trigger` (String) For `condition`: when the condition causes a send.
- `trigger_on_lower_band` (Boolean) For `anomaly_prophet`: send when the value is below the band. SELECT's default is true.
- `trigger_on_upper_band` (Boolean) For `anomaly_prophet`: send when the value is above the band. SELECT's default is true.
- `upper_percentile` (Number) For `anomaly_percentile`: the upper percentile of the band, from 0 to 100.

<a id="nestedatt--trigger_config--thresholds"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger_config.thresholds`

Required:

- `metric` (String) `actual_spend` or `forecast_spend`.
- `unit` (String) `percent` of the budget amount, or an `amount` of spend.
- `value` (Number) The percent or the amount.

## Import

`select_monitor` can be imported using the monitor's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_monitor.example 6c1f0e2a-3b4d-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b
```

To list the IDs, call `GET /v2/monitors`. See [IMPORT.md](https://github.com/get-select/terraform-provider-select/blob/main/IMPORT.md).

After an import, the first plan can show a change to `trigger_config`, `query_json` or `message_config_json`, because state holds the full document that SELECT stores. Write the configuration, then apply once.

## Additional Information

### `trigger_config` is one object, keyed by `type`

`trigger_config.type` selects the variant, and the other fields that are valid depend on it. A field that does not belong to the type fails at plan time:

| type | requires | accepts |
|---|---|---|
| `digest` | `skip_if_empty` | |
| `condition` | `query_json`, `operator`, `threshold`, `trigger` | |
| `anomaly_prophet` | `query_json`, `sensitivity` | `trigger_on_upper_band`, `trigger_on_lower_band`, `minimum_threshold` |
| `anomaly_percentile` | `query_json` | `upper_percentile`, `lower_percentile`, `deviations`, `minimum_threshold` |
| `budget_threshold` | `thresholds` | `query_json` |

### `query_json` and `message_config_json` are JSON documents

`trigger_config.query_json` is a `MonitorQuery` and `message_config_json` is a `MonitorMessageConfig`, both JSON-encoded. Use `jsonencode()`. `GET /v2/monitors/query-classes` lists the query classes, and `GET /v2/monitors/query-classes/{query_class}/columns` lists the columns of one class.

SELECT adds keys to these documents when it stores them: defaults such as `period.date_column`, and generated text such as a chart title or a paragraph body. The provider compares only the keys that the configuration sets. A key that only SELECT sets does not show as a change. A change to a key that the configuration sets shows as a change. A `null` in the configuration sets nothing, so a value that SELECT fills in for it does not show as a change.

The optional fields of `trigger_config` show a change when SELECT holds a value that the configuration does not set, with two exceptions. `trigger_on_upper_band` and `trigger_on_lower_band` do not show their default, `true`. An unset `query_json` on a `budget_threshold` trigger does not show a query that SELECT holds.

### An update replaces the full monitor

An update sends `PUT /v2/monitors/{id}` with the full configuration. Removing `cron`, `team_id`, `budget_id`, `snowflake_account_id` or `partition_columns` from the configuration clears it.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the monitor's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the monitor changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.
